3. Predict  
It is another goal of psychology.  To achieve this goal measurement i s necessary.  
Measurement of behavior serves as a primary basis for predicting what a person will do in the 
future.  With the help of school assessment we can predict a student's performance in college, and 
individual's score on a mechanical aptitude test.   We can predict his success on a particular job.  
4. Control  
Individual's behavior can be modified and controlled with the help of predi ction.  Psychologists 
want to change or modify the behavior of the individual in a way that is helpful.  Behavior change 
is the basic and aim of practicing psychologists.  
Psychotherapists try their best to change the patient's behavior.  The industrial psy chologist is 
engaged in an effort to modify the behavior of employees.  The marriage counselor attempts to 
modify the behavior of husband and wife.  In all of these cases an effort is made to improve the 
present or future circumstances of the individual an d society.   
Psychology must meet the challenge of application.  Being a student of psychology it must be our 
task to discover how to make the psychology relevant to our lives, how it can work for us.  We can 
learn the strategies to improve our study habit s, expands our memory span, effectively solve the 
problem, enhance self esteem, cope with stress, depression and much more.  We can also learn to 
control anger, overeating, smoking and poor - study habits with the help of psychology.

Goal of psychology is to describe explain, predict and control the behavior .  There is 
another goal i.e.  to improve the quality of human life.  Psychology wants to explain or understand 
why an individual behaves in a certain way and to predict how an individual will behave in the 
future.   
Let's discuss in detail the goals of ps ychology.   
1. Describe  
The first task of psychology is to get the facts or to collect the relevant data.  Actually data 
are the reports of observations.  As one ca n say that individual's feeling of anxiety can't be the data 
as they are unobservable.  But restless behavior, over secretion of epinephrine or verbal report of 
anxiety can be observed, measured and reported, it can be data about anxiety.   
In psychology d escription means the statements about the behavior of the organism and 
the conditions under which the behavior occurs.  Description is necessary for the understanding 
and manipulation of a phenomenon.  Psychologists spent a lot of time and effort in measuring and 
describing behavior.  Concepts like anxiety, I. Q, learning, attitude, abilities and depression must 
be measured that is why description is necessary.  
2. Explain  
Though description must stick to perceivable information, explanations deliberately go 
beyond.  It is done so to uncover the principles, processes or relationships tha t can be the causes.  
Some believe that explanation is really what basic research in psychology is all about.   
To explain and understand the behavior is a process which involves the theory formulation, 
organization of facts, and the hypotheses development  about the relationships that are yet to be 
proved.   
The psychologists may be able to describe and measure anxiety, to make predictions from 
the measurements.  Person's likelihood is predicted on the basis of measurement.  Psychologists 
seek to understand  the most complex part of the world i.e.  human being.

“Psychology is now defined as the scientific study of behavior and mental processes ” 
The word "psychology" comes from  Greek roots meaning "the study of soul or spirit".  The 
combination of two Greek letters "Psych" and "Logus" make the term psychology.  Psych means 
self, soul or mind and logus stands for knowledge.   
So psychology was defined as knowledge of soul, mind a nd consciousness in different eras.  
Let's discuss how these definitions restrict or help the field of psychology and  see if any one of 
them can enable us to understand what psychology is and what it deals with.  
1. Psychology as Science of Soul  
First of al l psychology was defined as "science of soul".  Soul is a concept we all know very well 
but can't describe easily, Muslims and non muslims both have clear concept according to their 
own belief  
This term has changed its meaning with the passage of time.  I n primitive era it was believed that 
each and everything has the soul, but afterwards this belief was limited to living organisms only.  
Another strong notion about soul is that it is immortal.  In Greek period concept of good and bad 
soul was prevailing y et Greek philosopher had described it by their own.  Let's discuss some of 
them.   
Greek philosophers  
 
1. Pythagoras  
He proposed that body is a prison for soul.  After the death of an individual soul becomes free and 
roam anywhere  according to its will  
2. Socrates  
 He was the first who introduced the word psyche.  He advocated that body is greater than soul.  
He believed that soul is immortal and not the  body. He said that everybody must seek the 
knowledge to make the sou l pure.   
3. Plato  
Plato  was in opinion that soul and body are separate system.  Both remain active and functioning 
till the last breadth.  He told that soul is just a shadow which can only be felt but no one can 
understand its reality.

Psychology as a science uses systematic methods to observe, describe, predict and explain the 
behavior.  Science is a method, which is systematic and objective.  Scientific methods are not 
casual, but researchers carefully and precisely, plan and conduct their studies.  In  psychology 
behavior is studied, experimented and analyzed.  For this purpose  psychologists use the same 
research methods as physicists biologists and other scientists.  So psychology claims itself as a 
science.   
Behavior:  
Behavior is everything we do that can be directly observed i.e.  laugh, run, cry, sleep, ride, write 
or drink . 
Mental Processes:  
Thoughts, feelings  and motives that each of us experience privately but that cannot be observed 
directly such as logical thinking, love, the inclination to study.  Psychologists explore them 
indirectly then infer information from observable behavior about the hidden behavio r which are 
the mental processes.

3.W. McDougall:  
He also adopted this definition for psychology.  
4.Thorndike  
who conducted many experiments on animals and introduced trial and error method for learning, 
is known as beha viorist  psychologist.  Pavlov and Skinner introduced the laws of conditioning 
while experimenting on animals.  With these rules human behavior can also be explained and 
controlled  
According to Watson individual learns from his environment.  He conducted successful 
experiments on small children and animals, and explained the Stimulus Response (SR) formula.  
Stimulus is studied as it elicits behavior, rewards and punishment to maintai n the responses, but S 
R is not concerned with what goes on inside the organism.  So it was criticized and amended as 
SOR.  Organism was included with stimulus and response.  
Behaviorists  conducted a lot of experiments and became dominated during the first  half of 
the 20th century.  Psychology has benefited from this definition Experimentation on behavior 
made the prediction easy.  But it is not enough to study the behavior only.  To cover the complete 
area of psychology this definition needs some additio n, 
Criticism  
1.Watson stressed on obvious behavior.  He did not realize the importance of mental processes.  2. 
Behavior seems just a mechanical response without mental process.   
3.Watson discarded the concepts of conscious, subconscious and unconscious  
4. Humanistic psychologists give a lot of importance to "intrinsic motivation", but behaviorists 
have no room for it.   
It is obvious that all definitions have some flaws because none of them cover the subject 
matter of psychology in a complete sense.  So definition given by behaviorists can be modified to 
meet the need.  If mental processes are included in it, then our criteria will be met.  
Comprehensive Definition  
Psychology is currently defined as the systematic and scientific study behavior, both anima l 
and human the term behavior refers to observable actions such as eating, speaking, and laughing 
as well as to mental activities such as planning, thinking and imagining.   
So psychology is the scientific study of behavior and mental processes.  There are  three 
key terms in this definition; Those  are science, behavior and mental processes.  Let's define them.
